programme.desc: Pascal Brodnicki likes to explore the world through his sense of taste.He loves to prepare various dishes at street stalls, in African villages or on the beach. However, during his culinary journeys it was not always easy for him.Sometimes elephants stole his ingredients.Of course, Pascal couldn't deny himself the pleasure of tasting local delicacies.In Delhi, he stopped for a long time at a paratha stand, in a Zanzibar village he ate rice with coconut, and in Namibia he tried a zebra steak."Taste the world with Pascal" is not only about cooking.The host visited an elephant orphanage in Sri Lanka, fed cheetahs in Africa and climbed a coconut tree.In Bombay he became a teacher and taught Polish to children, and on the coast of Zanzibar he hunted octopus.Everywhere his passion and positive energy attracted crowds of onlookers.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Kyoto is a city that was the capital of Japan for a thousand years.In addition to beautiful historic temples, there are fascinating "flower cities" - districts where you can meet "butterflies of the night", i.e. geisha.They look like women from out of this world - their white faces and colorful kimonos are hypnotizing.Martyna had the opportunity to visit this phenomenal city and meet 20-year-old Kimichie, who is currently a "maiko", which means that she is training to be a geisha.Many young Japanese women when asked "what do you want to be?"he will answer - "geisha".They think it's a calling.Viewers will learn why geishas whiten their faces and what their daily schedule is like.They will accompany them in their traditional activities, at the hairdresser's and shopping, and will also attend a party where geishas "work".The host will ask Kimicha many questions about their secrets.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Another woman Martyna Wojciechowska meets during her trip to Japan is 25-year-old Watanabe, a member of the himegyaru.This term describes girls and women styled as princesses - they wear tiaras, pink clothes and shiny jewelry, and their apartments look like Barbie doll houses.They are dominated by kawaii, i.e. everything that is sweet, nice and tiny.Watanabe will reveal to Martyna what she does every day.It will also help find the answer to the question why Japanese teenagers do not want to grow up and where the popularity of himegyaru comes from.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska has been wandering the world for many years and looking for interesting people who share their unique stories with her.The traveler not only talks about their everyday lives, but also raises important social issues.In the tenth season of the program he will visit, among others:Spitsbergen - the largest island of the Svalbard archipelago, where it is night for a quarter of the year.He will also reach out to the Wodaabe community living in Chad, and in El Salvador he will tackle the difficult issue of restrictive anti-abortion regulations. Martyna Wojciechowska breaks stereotypes.In the Wodaabe community of Chad, men court women.For this reason, they attach great importance to their appearance.They put on their best clothes and make up.Their chosen ones are only supposed to observe and then decide.The best place to look for a husband is the Gerewol Festival.The episode's heroine, Fatima, chose Haire last year.According to tradition, their wedding should take place on the anniversary of the happy event.A few months ago, the woman gave birth to a daughter.They only see each other in secret, because only such meetings are allowed.A man can have several wives, but he must pay appropriately for a good partner.Among the Wodaabe, the greatest wealth is cows.Haire's parents gave five cows and several million Central African francs for Fatima.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska has been wandering the world for many years and looking for interesting people who share their unique stories with her.The traveler not only talks about their everyday lives, but also raises important social issues.In the tenth season of the program he will visit, among others:Spitsbergen - the largest island of the Svalbard archipelago, where it is night for a quarter of the year.He will also reach out to the Wodaabe community living in Chad, and in El Salvador he will tackle the difficult issue of restrictive anti-abortion regulations. Martyna Wojciechowska spent six hundred and fifty days traveling, during which she visited fifty countries.This is how eighty episodes of the program were created.Over the ten years of the series, she has made many new friends, and many of the characters still hold a special place in her heart.They include Kabula - an albino girl from Tanzania.Thanks to the money collected by viewers and the "Between Heaven and Earth" foundation, she was able to fulfill her dreams.She started studying at a private school in Mwanza.Now he is doing everything he can to become a lawyer and defend the rights of people with albinism.She spent her last holidays in Poland, with Martyna Wojciechowska.Viewers will see how this first visit went.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska once again sets out on a fascinating journey to learn about different aspects of the lives of women living in distant corners of the world.Some of the points of the route in this edition will be India, Senegal, South Korea, South Africa, Israel and Mexico.The program participants will talk about their everyday lives and reveal intimate secrets to the traveler.Some of them will be truly moving.This season, the journalist will look at how the Orthodox Jewish community functions on a daily basis and how they celebrate the joyful holiday of Purim.He will visit a nursing home for women who were once involved in prostitution.Although this profession is legal in Mexico, women are not entitled to any benefits.The traveler will also meet teenage Karolina, who works almost 24 hours a day at a garbage dump, and in South Africa she will meet a girl who dives with sharks.These are just some of the many amazing experiences that await Martyna Wojciechowska Martyna Wojciechowska visits South Korea, a country that has one of the lowest fertility rates in the world.According to research, as much as 90 percentmen and 80 percentwomen between 25 and 30 are single.Women fear that marriage and pregnancy will stand in the way of their advancement at work and will be a reason for discrimination.On the other hand, South Korea is a conservative country and almost every woman wants to get married.For this reason, the business of solo weddings is booming here.It turns out that young Korean women do not even need a partner to fulfill their dreams of a white dress and a veil.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska once again sets out on a fascinating journey to learn about different aspects of the lives of women living in distant corners of the world.Some of the points of the route in this edition will be India, Senegal, South Korea, South Africa, Israel and Mexico.The program participants will talk about their everyday lives and reveal intimate secrets to the traveler.Some of them will be truly moving.This season, the journalist will look at how the Orthodox Jewish community functions on a daily basis and how they celebrate the joyful holiday of Purim.He will visit a nursing home for women who were once involved in prostitution.Although this profession is legal in Mexico, women are not entitled to any benefits.The traveler will also meet teenage Karolina, who works almost 24 hours a day at a garbage dump, and in South Africa she will meet a girl who dives with sharks.These are just some of the many amazing experiences that await Martyna Wojciechowska Martyna Wojciechowska's goal is Mexico.This is the country where most disappearances of women occur.Kidnapped or lured, they become part of one of the most profitable businesses - prostitution.The traveler visits the nursing home intended for them.Professional sex work is legal in Mexico, but women who engage in it cannot count on any pension or health benefits.At Casa Xochiquetzal, Martyna Wojciechowska talks to eighteen residents and the director of the home, who fights for them to age with dignity and to experience warmth.
